newsitem.title: JAPAN: US to ask Japan for more fiscal steps at G7 - source.
newsitem.headline: US to ask Japan for more fiscal steps at G7 - source.

text.p: The United States is likely to ask Japan to keep its easy monetary policy and take more fiscal steps to boost its economy at a bilateral meeting in Washington later this month, an international monetary source said on Wednesday.
"The U.S. will probably ask Japan to take both fiscal and monetary measures to support the economy," the source said.

U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin may make the requests if a meeting with Finance Minister Wataru Kubo is set to take place in Washington on the sidelines of the IMF/World Bank meetings starting later this week, he said.
Kubo is likely to say to Rubin that the BOJ may keep its current easy monetary stance, but that additional fiscal spending for the economy is unlikely, the source said.
Kubo has said Japan is plagued by a huge national debt, which has left its state budget in a critical state.
